cells.tense: The mind is lying still right now, and the direction comes out cleaner for it.
cells.act: go deeper into the shared thing than comfort allows
cells.ask: Take a subject the two of you skirt and stay in it past your usual exit — a second question, one more true sentence, once this week.
cells.core:
You can let the mind lie still and choose from there. When the hum quiets, direction comes out cleaner — this, not that, without the long argument first. That is what settling does for you, and it works often enough that you trust it.

Because it works, you skip steps other people take. Take a subject the two of you skirt and stay in it past your usual exit. A second question. One more true sentence, once this week. Walk back with a little more of what holds you two together, said where the other person can hear it. Some things stay unsaid. The part you crossed toward is yours to keep.
cells.sheetLine: Stillness does its work. Take one of you deeper with it.

cells.tense: The direction is settled in the mind, and it will be defended hard before anything real has happened.
cells.act: gather your determination and hold the line
cells.ask: When the next pull off course arrives, stay on your heading without rearguing the case to yourself. No announcement needed.
cells.core:
A direction got chosen. The mind ran the scenarios, settled on one, and now spends energy defending it against pushback that hasn't arrived. Warnings rehearsed for choices nobody has challenged. The heading is real; most of the defending is not.

What feeds a direction is how you actually feel about it, not the rehearsals. Gather what you have and hold the line once for real. When the next pull off course arrives, stay on your heading without rearguing the case in your head. Nobody has to hear about it. See what the push actually is. Whatever it turns out to be, the direction stays yours.
cells.sheetLine: The heading is real. The defending got there first.

cells.tense: The deciding had gone quiet, and standing somewhere new, the mind kept waiting at the old door.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Something is pulling at you a little. Follow it a short way and stop where you like — no verdict, no deadline, nobody told.
cells.core:
Somewhere in the last stretch, the deciding stopped. The mind settled, and settling turned into sitting still — the old direction still warm, the new one not tried. Nothing seemed worth a this, not that. That happens in a life without anything being wrong; the quiet just outlasted its use.

Here is the small way back. Something is pulling at you a little. Follow it a short way and stop wherever you like — no verdict owed, nobody told, no clock on it. The pull does the walking; you are just not stepping on it. Where it lets you go is far enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: The quiet outlasted the deciding. Follow one pull.

cells.tense: Steering is happening now, quietly, and the hands on the wheel are filed under something other than you.
cells.act: cross over to the people it actually requires
cells.ask: Think of the last turn you made because of someone close to you, and say the plain truth of it aloud — one line, to yourself if that is all.
cells.core:
The quiet is going into steering, and the credit is landing elsewhere. You settle around a direction, hold it, adjust it, and the whole thing gets filed under the people near you wanting it, or luck, or the way things happen to fall. That isn't how it went. Nobody is being named as the one who turned it, and yet the direction keeps moving.

Name that turn. Think of the last time you changed course because of someone close to you, and say the plain truth of it aloud — what you did, one line, to yourself if that is all it takes. That is the crossing, and it was yours. The hands are yours too.
cells.sheetLine: Name the last turn you made. It was yours.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that when the mind stays quiet it is healing on purpose: the state is observable, the purpose is not, and the person reserves the right to say it is fog rather than recovery. The likely objection is that thinking is the one thing they cannot put down. The asks survive a wrong read in the kinds of Things They Carry, Witness Your Turning, and In Their Company — presence and memory do not require the diagnosis to be right — while Keep it unspent needs the quiet to exist. The sentence that serves the writer over the person is 'your stillness has a purpose'; it will be cut, and the offer will say what they walked back with and why, not for what.
